Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:10:1.english: It is [a dispute between] tanna’im - This is our reading.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:10:2.hebrew: אמר ר' טרפון - לאנשי ביתו: הזהרו בי, להיות עמי ועם כלתי, שלא אתייחד עמה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:10:2.english: Rabbi Tarfon said - [He said this] to the members of his household: Be careful with me, to be with me and with my daughter-in-law, so that I will not be secluded with her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:11:1.hebrew: מכלליה מכולה דברא - כשהיה הולך בשדה בגירסא, לייחוד היה מונע הבהמות מכל השדה. ד"א: שאינו מניח להיות רועה והבהמות בשדה אחד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:11:1.english: Kept [them] away from the entire field - When he would walk in the field [engaged] in study, [out of concern for] seclusion he would keep the animals away from the entire field. Another explanation: That he would not allow a shepherd and the animals to be in one field.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:12:1.hebrew: שתי יבמות - נשי שני אחין, ששונאות זו את זו כשתי צרות, שדואגות שמא תפול ליבום לפני בעלה ותיעשה לה צרה. אשה וצרתה, ואשה וחמותה, ובת חמותה, ובת בעלה — כולן שונאות זו את זו, וטעמא מפרש ביבמות, בפרק האשה שהלכה (יבמות דף קיז.):
Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:12:1.english: Two sisters-in-law - [The] wives of two brothers, who hate each other like two rival wives, as they worry lest [the other] fall to levirate marriage [yibbum] before her husband and become a rival wife to her. A woman and her rival wife, and a woman and her mother-in-law, and [a woman and] the daughter of her mother-in-law, and [a woman and] her husband's daughter — all of them hate each other. And the reason is explained in Yevamot, in the chapter [entitled] HaIsha SheHalcha (Yevamot 117a).

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:12:2.hebrew: שיודעת טעם ביאה - כלומר, מה היא ביאה, שתדע לספר דברים בשוק:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:12:2.english: Who knows the meaning of intercourse - That is to say, what intercourse is, so that she will know to recount things in the marketplace.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:12:3.hebrew: ואינה מוסרת עצמה לביאה - מתוך קוטנה, עדיין לא לבשה יצר. הילכך, אין כאן משום דעת קלה, שלא תהא נוחה להתפתות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:12:3.english: And she does not submit herself to intercourse - Due to her youth, she has not yet taken on the [evil] inclination. Therefore, there is no [concern] here on account of [women having] a light mind, as she is not easily seduced.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:13:1.hebrew: תינוקת בת תשע שנים ויום אחד - והביאה שערות, דכי איכא "שדים נכונו ושערך צמח" — הוא דמגרו בה. וסבר לה כמאן דאמר (בנדה דף מו.): בת תשע שנים ויום אחד שהביאה שערות — סימן הן מכאן ואילך, אבל קודם לכן — שומא. ותינוק בן י"ב שנה ויום אחד — קרי ליה "הגדיל", ולא יישן עם אמו עוד בקירוב בשר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:13:1.english: A girl of nine years and one day - And [this applies provided] that she has developed [pubertal] hair, for only when [the stage of] “your bosom was fashioned and your hair had grown” (Ezekiel 16:7) is reached does temptation become a concern regarding her. And he holds in accordance with the one who said (in Niddah 46a): With a girl of nine years and one day who developed hair, from this point forward they are considered a [valid halakhic] sign [of maturity], but prior to this, [it is merely regarded as] a mole. And a boy of twelve years and one day [the Mishnah] terms “grown up,” and he may no longer share a bed with his mother in direct bodily contact [without clothing].

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:13:2.hebrew: זה וזה - בין ללישנא קמא, בין ללישנא בתרא דתינוקת — בעינן "שדים נכונו", בסימני נערות, בסימנין [שבדדים], דהיינו בוחל, כדתנן במסכת נדה (דף מז.): "בוחל — אלו ימי הנעורים", ו"שערך צמח". אלא דללישנא קמא, אי אתיא שערות מתשע שנים ולמעלה — הוי סימן גמור; וללישנא בתרא — הוי שומא עד בת שתים עשרה שנים ויום אחד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:13:2.english: This and that - Both according to the first version and according to the latter version regarding a female child, we require [both] “breasts were fashioned” — [manifested] in the signs of maidenhood, in the signs [on the breasts], which is bochel [the ripening stage], as we learned in a mishna in tractate Niddah (47a): “Bochel — these are the days of maidenhood” — and “your hair was grown.” Except that according to the first version, if she grew [pubic] hairs from nine years [of age] and above, it is a valid sign; whereas according to the latter version, it is [considered merely] a mole until she is twelve years and one day old.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:14:1.english: Ashamed to stand before him - It is known that she has an awareness of intercourse.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:15:1.hebrew: לא סבר לה מר דמקדשא - אין אדוני יודע שהיא מקודשת, ויש לו להתרחק מאשת איש:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:15:1.english: Does the Master not think that she is betrothed - Does my master not know that she is betrothed, and [therefore] he must distance himself from a married woman?

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:1:1.hebrew: תיב שפיר - שב כהוגן, שלא תמאיסנו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:1:1.english: Sit properly - Sit properly, so that you do not disgust us.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:1:10.english: Hid - He hid in a bathroom outside the city.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:1:11.english: He saw him - Satan [saw] Peleimu, that he was suffering.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:1:12.english: What is the reason that you spoke this way - Why were you accustomed to curse me?

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:1:13.hebrew: אלא היכי נימא - לדחותך מעלי, שלא תחטיאני:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:1:13.english: Rather, how should we say - To push you away from me, so that you do not cause me to sin:

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:1:2.english: Give me a cup - Pour for me a cup [of wine].

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:1:3.hebrew: אכמר - שוטי"ר (טושי"ר: להשתעל), בלע"ז:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:1:3.english: He became hot and inflamed - Shotir (toshir: to cough), in the vernacular.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:1:4.hebrew: שדא ביה כיחו - השליך בתוכו את כיחו, ליחה היוצאה מן הריאה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:1:4.english: He threw his phlegm into it - He cast his phlegm into it — mucus that emerges from the lungs.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:1:5.english: They berated him - They rebuked him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:1:6.english: He sank - He pretended to be dead.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:1:8.hebrew: שמעו דקאמרי פלימו קטל גברא - השמיעו לאנשי ביתו קול יוצא מבחוץ, ואומרים: ״פלימו קטל גברא״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:1:8.english: They heard that they were saying: “Peleimu killed a man” - They caused the members of his household to hear a voice coming from outside, and [people] saying: “Peleimu killed a man!”

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:1:9.hebrew: ערק - פלימו, כסבור שבאים עליו נוגשי המלך להורגו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:1:9.english: He fled - Peleimu, believing that the king's officers were coming upon him to kill him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:2:1.hebrew: דפריש מינאי - מחמת זקנה, ומה ירא מיצר הרע:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:2:1.english: That he separated from me - Due to old age; and why is he afraid of the evil inclination?

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:3:1.hebrew: קשטה נפשה - בתכשיטיה, קישוטי בשמים ואפרסמון:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:3:1.english: She adorned herself - With her adornments — adornments of perfumes and balsam.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:3:2.english: She passed and repeated before him - She passed before him and repeated [it] a second time.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:3:3.hebrew: דפריש מינאי - מחמת זקנה, ומה ירא מיצר הרע:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:3:3.english: That he has separated from me - On account of old age; and what does he fear from the evil inclination?

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:3:4.english: I am Ḥaruta - The name of a prostitute well-known in the city.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:3:5.english: That I returned today - That I returned here today:

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:3:6.english: [That is at the] top of the bough - A small branch at the top of the palm tree.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:4:1.english: He sat inside it - To put himself to death.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:5:1.english: Her husband has made them null - [Those who intended to transgress] require forgiveness.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:5:2.hebrew: במה הכתוב מדבר - מאחר שאישה הפרה, מה שעברה? ומה זו סליחה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:5:2.english: With regard to what is the verse speaking? - Since her husband nullified [her vows], what did she transgress, and what is this forgiveness [for]?

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:5:3.hebrew: והיא שותה ביין - מיד, ואף על פי שבהיתר, כיון שהיא לאיסור נתכוונה — צריכה סליחה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:5:3.english: And she drank wine - Immediately; and even though [it was] permitted, since she intended [to commit] a prohibition, she requires forgiveness.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:6:1.hebrew: אמר ר' טרפון - לאנשי ביתו: "הזהרו בי" — להיות עמי ועם כלתי, שלא אתייחד עמה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:6:1.english: Rabbi Tarfon said - [He said] to the members of his household: "Watch over me" — to be with me and with my daughter-in-law, so that I will not be secluded with her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:7:1.hebrew: כל הדווים - שיש להם לב לדוות, ידוו על זה — שאינו מתכוין, ויש כאן נשיאות עון:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:7:1.english: All who grieve - [Those] who have a heart to grieve shall grieve over this — that [even when] one does not intend [to sin], there is bearing of iniquity here.

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:8:1.hebrew: ודר עם אמו או עם בתו - דלא תקיף יצריה עלייהו, דאהנו ביה אנשי כנסת הגדולה דלא מגרי בקרובתא, מכי כחלינהו ונקרינהו לעיניה כו' (סנהדרין דף סד.):
Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:8:1.english: And live with his mother or with his daughter - For his [evil] inclination is not strong toward them, as the Men of the Great Assembly were effective regarding it [such] that it does not incite [desire] toward relatives, ever since they put kohl in its eyes and gouged them out, etc. (Sanhedrin 64a).

Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:8:2.hebrew: מתייחד עם אחותו - לפרקים, אבל אינו דר תמיד ביחוד אצלה בבית:
Rashi on Kiddushin 81b:8:2.english: [A man] may be secluded with his sister - Occasionally, but he may not live permanently in seclusion with her in the house.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 81b:11:1.hebrew: אביי מכלי להו מכולה דברא - נראה דהני אמוראי חומרא בעלמא קא עבדי, ואנן קיימא לן כרבנן דרבי יהודה (לקמן קידושין דף פב.) דאמרו לו: "לא נחשדו ישראל לא על משכב זכור ולא על הבהמה":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 81b:11:1.english: "Abaye removed them from the entire field" - It appears that these Amoraim were merely acting stringently, and we hold in accordance with the Rabbis [who dispute] Rabbi Yehuda (below, Kiddushin 82a), who said to him: "Israelites are not suspected of homosexual intercourse or of bestiality."
